text.stageNote: In the order of the stay, from the booking to the close of the audit.
tips: Log it the night you find it.
The audit is the one moment the whole day is checked. An exception written the next morning has lost its room number, its time and its reason.
One no-show is one reservation, whatever the rate. The lost revenue goes in the cost box, so both are kept.
Without the arrivals and in-house reservations of the day you see counts; with them you get a rate, DPMO and sigma level, and a week with 300 arrivals compares with a week with 120.
text.checkIntro: Tick what was actually done tonight, not what the night audit procedure says. Every unticked line is a place where an exception can start, or where one is found too late.

Booking.meaning: An exception found at the booking stage was born before the guest arrived: a rate, a date or a guarantee that was wrong in the reservation and nobody read it before the night.
moves: Check tomorrow's arrivals during the evening shift: rate, guarantee, special requests, and fix what is wrong while the booking source can still be reached.
Keep “arrived with a wrong booking” apart from “booked wrong here” in the log, so the channel or the agent that sends the errors can be shown the numbers.
Share the booking errors with reservations and sales every week, with the reservation numbers.
Booking.question: Who reads tomorrow's arrivals before the night, and what do they check?

Arrival.meaning: At check-in the guest is in front of the desk: a missing registration card, a guarantee not taken or a no-show not released starts here, at the busiest hour of the evening.
moves: Make the registration card and the card guarantee the first two steps of every check-in, before the key is cut.
Release the no-shows at a fixed time, with the cancellation policy applied the same way every night.
Walk the arrivals list at the end of the late shift: every expected guest is either in-house, a no-show or a cancellation, never still “expected”.
Arrival.question: What does the desk do when a guest arrives without a valid card during the evening rush?

In-house.meaning: Exceptions in-house are postings: a breakfast, a minibar or a parking fee on the wrong room, a rate that did not roll over, a charge posted twice.
moves: Compare the postings of the day with the outlets' own lists before the audit runs, not after the invoice is printed.
Post to the room, not to the name: two guests with the same name are the oldest posting error there is.
Check the rate code of every in-house room against the reservation once a night; a changed rate shows up here first.
In-house.question: Which outlet's postings land on the wrong room most often, and at which hour?

Payment.meaning: A declined card, a virtual card that fails or a pre-authorisation that was never taken: money that the hotel will chase tomorrow instead of having tonight.
moves: Pre-authorise every card at check-in and record the authorisation code on the reservation.
Charge virtual cards on arrival, not at departure; a failed VCC is reported to the booking channel the same night.
Keep a list of the declined cards with the guest's reply, so the morning shift knows who to ask and what was already tried.
Payment.question: Which reservations go to sleep tonight with no valid payment behind them?

Departure.meaning: At check-out the exception becomes visible to the guest: an open balance, a dispute over a posting, an invoice with the wrong address or company.
moves: Prepare the invoices of tomorrow's departures during the night audit and read each one once.
Settle the open balances of the day before the audit closes, or name who follows up and by when.
Ask for the invoice address at check-in, when the guest has time, not at the taxi.
Departure.question: How many of tomorrow's invoices have been read by someone before the guest sees them?

Audit close.meaning: Found at the close of the audit means found by the system, not by a person: an unbalanced report, a room without a rate, a posting that would not roll over.
moves: Run the pre-audit checks an hour before the close, so what they find can still be fixed tonight.
Keep the reasons the audit would not balance in the log, with the room: the same three usually return.
Close with a short written note to the morning shift: what was fixed, what stays open and who owns it.
Audit close.question: What stopped the audit from closing cleanly this week, and how often was it the same thing?

causes.Booking data: The booking itself was wrong: rate, dates, guarantee or guest details. Show the booking source its own numbers every week; most errors come from one or two channels.
causes.No guarantee: A reservation without a valid card or a prepayment is a no-show waiting to happen. Make the guarantee a condition of the booking, not a request at check-in.
causes.Handover gap: The late shift knew and the night did not, or the night knew and the morning did not. Put it on the shift handover, with a name and a time.
causes.System: Rate codes, interfaces and the audit itself fail in patterns. Write down the exact error and the room; a vendor fixes what is documented.
causes.Guest: The guest did not show, did not pay or disputed a charge. Record what was agreed with them, so the next shift does not start the conversation again.
causes.Training: The posting was made by hand and made wrong. Watch the step once with the person, then fix the step: a checklist at the desk beats a reminder in the meeting.
causes.Unknown: A large Unknown share means the log is not yet good enough. Record stage and cause at the moment the exception is found, during the audit.

checklist: Tomorrow's arrivals were checked during the evening: rate, guarantee and special requests.
Every expected guest is in-house, a no-show or a cancellation; nobody is still “expected”.
No-shows were released at the agreed time, with the cancellation policy applied the same way.
Every in-house room has a valid rate code and a registration card on file.
Every card was pre-authorised at check-in and the authorisation is on the reservation.
Virtual cards of today's arrivals were charged tonight, and the failed ones reported to the channel.
Postings of the day were compared with the outlets' lists before the audit ran.
Tomorrow's invoices were prepared and read once during the night.
The pre-audit checks ran before the close, and what they found was fixed or handed over.
The morning shift has a written note: what was fixed, what stays open and who owns it.
